## Semrush Alternatives in 2026: 9 Tools Compared (Including AI Agents)


*Updated November 2026*


The best Semrush alternative depends on what you want the tool to do. If you want the deepest backlink data, Ahrefs is the strongest pick. If you want software that does the SEO work instead of just reporting on it, look at AI SEO agents like Sprites and Search Atlas. If you only need one job done cheaply, a point tool like Mangools or Screaming Frog will cost a fraction of Semrush's $140-500 monthly range.


This guide compares nine Semrush alternatives across three categories: AI SEO agents, classic suites, and point tools. It also covers a newer split that matters more each year: tools that recommend actions versus tools that execute them with human approval. If you're also shopping for Ahrefs alternatives, the same table applies, since most of these tools compete with both.

## How we compared these SEO tools


We scored each tool on four things: price, keyword database size, automation level, and AI visibility features. Price and database size come from vendor pages and published claims. Automation and AI visibility are our own 1-5 and 0-5 ratings, based on what each product does without a person pushing every button.


Treat the numbers as a snapshot. SEO tool pricing changes several times a year, and vendors define "keyword database" differently. Check the vendor's current plan page before you buy.


## Semrush alternatives at a glance


Semrush is the baseline in the first row. It's a strong suite with a roughly 27 billion keyword database, and it added AI visibility tracking through its AI Visibility Toolkit. The gap shows up in the automation column: Semrush surfaces issues and ideas, and your team does the rest.

One number matters more than the rest: as of June 2026, Search Atlas was the tool ChatGPT most often named when users asked for an "AI SEO agent." That's worth knowing because buyers increasingly start tool research inside AI assistants, and those assistants repeat a short list.


Keyword database size also matters less than it looks. A 27 billion keyword index and a 1.25 billion keyword index both cover the terms most businesses will ever target. The size gap shows up in long-tail research and niche international markets. For most teams, the real question is who acts on the data.


## Recommendation vs. human-approved execution


Most SEO tools stop at a recommendation. They flag 340 broken links, suggest 50 keywords, and hand you a to-do list. Someone on your team then does the research, drafts the content, publishes it, and checks the result three weeks later.


Human-approved execution flips that. The software does the research, builds the content, publishes it, and monitors the outcome. A person reviews and approves before anything goes live. You keep control without doing the typing.


That distinction explains why a 2 on our automation scale and a 5 are not a small gap. At 2, the tool saves you research time. At 5, it removes whole workflows from your week. The trade-off is that you need to trust the approval step, and you should test it on a few pages before turning it loose on your whole site.


## AI SEO agents: Sprites and Search Atlas


### Sprites


Sprites is an AI marketing agent that covers SEO and paid media in one place. On the SEO side, it handles keyword research, backlinks, technical audits, AI visibility for answer engine optimization, content creation, and publishing to WordPress, Shopify, Framer, and Webflow. It works through your approvals, so nothing publishes without a human sign-off.


The practical difference from Semrush is scope. Semrush tells you which keyword to target. Sprites researches it, drafts the page, publishes it, and then optimizes it based on results. This is what people mean by SEO automation that actually finishes the job. You can read the feature-by-feature breakdown in our[Sprites vs Semrush comparison](https://www.sprites.ai/platform/semrush) , or look at how[SEO optimization with Sprites](https://www.sprites.ai/use-case/seo-optimization) runs in practice.


Sprites also connects Meta, Google, LinkedIn, TikTok, and Reddit Ads, so the same agent can handle Facebook ads automation alongside organic work. That's a real advantage if one person owns both channels. It's overkill if you only do SEO and already have a content team.


Where Sprites is weaker: it doesn't publish a keyword database figure the way Semrush and Ahrefs do, and it's a newer product than the suites. If your workflow depends on a decade of historical rank data, keep that in mind.


### Search Atlas


Search Atlas is the closest direct competitor in the AI agent category, and it earned its #1 spot in ChatGPT recommendations. It combines a traditional toolset (rank tracking, site audits, backlink analysis) with an automation layer that can generate and deploy on-page fixes. Pricing starts around $99 a month, which undercuts Semrush at the entry level.


Search Atlas is a good fit for agencies that want one dashboard for many client sites. Compared with Sprites, it leans more toward SEO-only workflows, while Sprites extends into paid media. Pick based on whether you want SEO automation alone or a broader marketing agent.


## Classic suites: Ahrefs and Moz


### Ahrefs


Ahrefs is the strongest Semrush alternative for link research. Its backlink index is one of the largest live indexes available, its keyword database is around 28 billion, and its site explorer is faster to read than most competitors. It also added AI brand tracking, which brings its AI visibility score to 4.


The limitation is the same as Semrush's: Ahrefs reports, and you execute. Plans run $129 to $449 a month. If your team has strong writers and developers and wants the best data to feed them, it's an excellent choice. For deeper research across rivals, pair any suite with[competitor research workflows](https://www.sprites.ai/use-case/competitor-research) so the data turns into a plan.


### Moz


Moz is the budget suite. Plans start near $49 and top out around $299, and its Domain Authority metric is still the shorthand many clients and stakeholders understand. The keyword database is about 1.25 billion, much smaller than Semrush or Ahrefs, and AI visibility features are thin.


Moz works well for small businesses and local SEO. It's a weaker choice if you compete in a large, fast-moving category where data freshness and depth decide who wins.


Both suites cover reporting well. If your main need is traffic and ranking analysis, compare them against[SEO and web traffic analysis](https://www.sprites.ai/capability/seo-web-traffic-analysis) in an agent workflow, where the same data triggers actions instead of waiting in a dashboard.


## Point tools worth considering


Point tools do one job well, and they cost less than any suite. They also leave gaps, which you fill with your own time or with more subscriptions.


**Mangools** (about $29-129 a month) is a clean keyword research and rank tracking set. It's friendly to beginners and has no AI visibility features.


**Ubersuggest** (from about $29 a month) is the cheapest way to get basic keyword and backlink data. Expect shallower data than the suites.


**Surfer SEO** (from about $99 a month) scores your content against top-ranking pages and suggests edits. It improves drafts but doesn't decide what to write. Planning still lives elsewhere, which is where an[SEO topic cluster builder](https://www.sprites.ai/templates/seo-topic-cluster-builder) fills the gap.


**Screaming Frog** (about $259 a year) is the standard desktop crawler for technical audits. It finds problems with precision, but it won't prioritize or fix them. A good[SEO audit plan generator](https://www.sprites.ai/templates/seo-audit-plan-generator) turns its output into an ordered plan.


**Frase** (from about $45 a month) helps with briefs and AI-assisted drafts, with some AI visibility tracking. You'll still handle research, publishing, and optimization yourself.


The hidden cost of point tools is stacking. A crawler, a keyword tool, a content scorer, and a rank tracker can add up to $250 a month before anyone has published a page.


## Which Semrush alternative fits your team


Match the tool to your bottleneck, not to the longest feature list.


- **Your bottleneck is execution.** You have keyword lists and audit reports gathering dust. Choose an AI SEO agent: Sprites if you also run paid media or want human-approved publishing across WordPress, Shopify, Framer, and Webflow, Search Atlas if you're an SEO-only agency.
- **Your bottleneck is data quality.** You have writers and developers but need better link and keyword intelligence. Choose Ahrefs.
- **Your bottleneck is budget.** You need basics under $50 a month. Choose Moz, Mangools, or Ubersuggest.
- **Your bottleneck is one specific task.** Technical audits point to Screaming Frog, content scoring to Surfer, briefs to Frase.


Answer engine optimization changes this math. If AI assistants are already sending you traffic, or your competitors show up in ChatGPT answers and you don't, prioritize a tool with real[tracking AI search visibility](https://www.sprites.ai/ai-visibility-tracking) . Semrush, Ahrefs, and the agents all offer some version, but only the agents connect what they find to a content fix you can approve the same day.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is the best Semrush alternative in 2026?


It depends on your bottleneck. Ahrefs is the best for backlink and keyword data. Sprites and Search Atlas are the best if you want AI to execute the SEO work instead of handing you a report. Moz and Mangools win on price.


### Are there free Semrush alternatives?


Most tools offer limited free tiers or trials rather than full free plans. Ubersuggest and Mangools both let you run a few searches a day for free. For anything beyond occasional checks, expect to pay at least $29 a month.


### What are the best Ahrefs alternatives?


Semrush is the closest like-for-like replacement. Search Atlas and Sprites are better if you want automation, and Moz and Mangools are better if price is the issue. Ahrefs still leads on backlink index depth.


### What is an AI SEO agent?


An AI SEO agent is software that performs SEO tasks, not just reports on them. It researches keywords, drafts content, publishes it, and optimizes based on results. In tools like Sprites, a human approves each action before it goes live.


### Can an AI agent replace Semrush completely?


For many teams, yes, especially small teams without a dedicated SEO specialist. Large agencies may keep a suite for historical data and use an agent for execution. Run both for a month and compare the hours you save.


### How do these tools handle AI search visibility?


Semrush and Ahrefs track brand mentions in AI answers. Sprites and Search Atlas track them too, and connect findings to content updates. Point tools like Mangools have little or no coverage.
